::: {.why}
Most published comparisons lose here by tuning the complicated model carefully and the simple one not at all, and milestone 7 is specifically graded on not doing that.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Tune a regularized linear model as carefully as you intend to tune anything else, and report its out-of-sample performance with an interval.
- Say which regularizer you chose and defend it from the correlation structure of your features.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Fit ridge, lasso and elastic net under the frozen protocol with the purged splitter, tuning the penalty properly inside each training fold rather than once globally. Report out-of-sample R-squared and information ratio with intervals from the effective sample size.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Defend the choice from the data: report the condition number and the correlation structure of your feature matrix, and say which regularizer that argues for. With eight correlated signals, lasso's tendency to pick one from a correlated group is a defect rather than a feature, and elastic net is usually the right default for that reason.
:::
:::

## The running strategy

::: {.project}
The linear baseline is fitted and tuned under the frozen protocol with nested penalty selection, and its interval is the bar every later model in the phase is measured against.
:::
